title: SELinuxMount is on by default — pods that set seLinuxOptions and share volumes with differently-labelled pods lose access

detection.reason: the conflict is between two pods sharing one volume with different labels, on an SELinux-enforcing node; the projection has hasSeLinuxOptions per pod but not the volume identity or the node's SELinux mode, so the pods that set a label are the candidates

quote: The feature is enabled by default in `v1.37`, which may break existing workloads in clusters with SELinux enabled.
remediation: Only clusters whose nodes enforce SELinux are affected (the cluster-wide advisory `rtz-k8s-advisory-selinuxmount-ga-1.37` says why). For each named pod, check whether another pod with a different SELinux label mounts the same volume; the 1.36 kubelet reports such conflicts via the `volume_manager_selinux_volume_context_mismatch_errors_total` metric. Fix the labels, or set `seLinuxChangePolicy: Recursive` on the pod to opt out of the mount-option relabel.
verifyCommand: for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do echo "== $n"; kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$n/proxy/metrics" | grep '^volume_manager_selinux_volume_context_mismatch'; done  # a non-zero mismatch counter on an SELinux node is a workload that breaks at 1.37

title: Kubelet logs its effective configuration at startup — restrict nodes/log to trusted principals

detection.reason: every cluster grants nodes/log to some system role, so the presence of the grant is not a finding; the question is WHO holds it, which is a binding-level audit

quote: Because these logs can expose configuration details, cluster administrators should restrict the `nodes/logs` ClusterRole to trusted users.
remediation: Audit which subjects can read `nodes/log` (and `nodes/proxy`); anything beyond cluster administrators and the logging stack should lose it before the kubelets are upgraded.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.roleRef.name as $r | (["cluster-admin","system:kubelet-api-admin"] | index($r)) != null) | .metadata.name + ": " + ([.subjects[]? | .kind + "/" + .name] | join(","))'  # subjects that can read kubelet logs after the upgrade

title: PodCertificateRequest v1 drops PKIXPublicKey and ProofOfPossession — signer controllers on the v1beta1 fields must be updated

detection.reason: PodCertificateRequests are not collected and the signer implementation is a runtime behaviour

quote: The `PKIXPublicKey` and `ProofOfPossession` fields, deprecated in PodCertificateRequest `v1beta1`, are removed from the `v1` API. Update clients that still set these fields before upgrading.
remediation: Only clusters that enabled the beta PodCertificateRequest feature and run a custom signer are affected; upgrade the signer to read `spec.stubPKCS10Request` before the control plane moves to 1.37.
verifyCommand: kubectl get podcertificaterequests -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.pkixPublicKey != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " signer=" + .spec.signerName'  # requests still carrying the removed fields

title: cloud-controller-manager config: NodeSyncPeriod moved to NodeLifecycleController.NodeMonitorPeriod

detection.reason: the cloud-controller-manager configuration lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

remediation: A cloud-controller-manager configuration file (or a provider that vendors the config type) setting `KubeCloudShared.NodeSyncPeriod` must move the value; the `--node-sync-period` flag is unchanged. Only clusters running an external cloud-controller-manager built on the 1.37 libraries are affected.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=cloud-controller-manager -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[] | .image, (.args[]? // empty)' | grep -i 'image\|node-sync\|config'  # a --config file is where the moved field would live

title: metrics.k8s.io graduates to v1 — the registered metrics-server APIService still serves only v1beta1
quote: Promoted the `metrics.k8s.io` API from `v1beta1` to `v1` without changes.
remediation: Clients built against 1.37 libraries prefer `metrics.k8s.io/v1`; a metrics-server release that registers only `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` keeps working for clients that fall back to v1beta1, but `kubectl top`, the HPA controller and dashboards should be verified after the upgrade. Plan a metrics-server release that registers `v1.metrics.k8s.io`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get apiservices -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group == "metrics.k8s.io") | .metadata.name + " available=" + (.status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "Available") | .status)'  # no v1.metrics.k8s.io row means the installed metrics-server predates the v1 API

title: Empty pod-level resources no longer drive the QoS class

detection.reason: the projection does not distinguish an empty pod-level resources block from an absent one

quote: Empty Pod resources (`{}`, `{requests:{}}`, or `{limits:{}}`) no longer affect QoS calculation.
remediation: A pod with an empty `spec.resources` block was classified from that block; from 1.37 its QoS comes from the containers, so the class (and eviction order) of such pods can change when they are recreated. Remove the empty block or set real pod-level values.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.resources != null and ((.spec.resources.requests // {}) == {}) and ((.spec.resources.limits // {}) == {})) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " qos=" + .status.qosClass'  # pods whose QoS may change on recreation

title: CEL == on x-kubernetes-list-type set/map lists no longer matches lists with duplicates — CRD and admission-policy verdicts can change

detection.reason: CRD schemas are collected only as group/versions; the validation rules inside a schema are not projected

quote: Equality (`==`) no longer matches lists containing duplicates, and concatenation (`+`) correctly applies set and map merge semantics to appended elements.
remediation: Re-check `x-kubernetes-validations` rules and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy expressions that compare or concatenate list fields declared `x-kubernetes-list-type: set` or `map`: an object that passed because a duplicate-bearing list compared equal is rejected after the upgrade, and `+` now de-duplicates.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crds -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.. | objects | select(has("x-kubernetes-validations") and (.["x-kubernetes-list-type"]? == "set" or .["x-kubernetes-list-type"]? == "map"))] | length != 0) | .metadata.name'  # CRDs with CEL rules on set/map lists; review each rule's == and +
coversNotes: Fixed CEL for "set" and "map" lists: equality (`==`) no longer matches lists containing

title: kube-apiserver validates --advertise-address against the Endpoints reconciler at startup

detection.reason: the --advertise-address flag lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

quote: Kube-apiserver now validates the `--advertise-address` IP when using `--endpoint-reconciler-type` `master-count` or `lease` to ensure the specified IP address can be persisted to an `Endpoints` API object successfully.
remediation: An advertise address that is not a valid Endpoints address (unspecified `0.0.0.0`, a loopback, link-local or multicast address, or one inside the Service CIDR) stops the 1.37 kube-apiserver at startup instead of failing silently later; set it to the node's routable IP.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?' | grep -E -- '--(advertise-address|endpoint-reconciler-type)'  # the address must be a routable unicast IP outside the Service CIDR
